feedback: Iteration 0 is the only race evidence. All 60 trials ended off_track with one line-loss event each, and RMS error stayed near 0.03. That points to coverage at the sensor row edges, not tracking precision: the outer sensors at x = 0.024 stop seeing the 25 mm tape beyond about 0.0425 m offset, and the robot runs off after losing the line. Your +/-0.05 m span addresses this directly, which I have built into the controller. From the controller side, widening the row lowers the signal change per millimetre of offset, so the steering gain is somewhat weaker than in the baseline; I kept kp at 3.0 to isolate the sensing change. I have not seen per-step telemetry or any evidence of outer-sensor saturation, so I am not able to confirm the saturation risk you raised in iteration 0. For the next proposal, decide from the next race. If line_loss_events are still above about 0.5 per run with the wider span, hold the geometry and check the controller's line recovery before changing sensors. If max_error comes close to 0.06 without line loss, the 16 mm footprint (coverage about 0.0685 m + 0.002 m) is worth trying so the outer sensors reach further, but only if rms_error is low. If line loss is gone and steering_oscillation rises, the longer look-ahead (y near 0.06) is the next option.
requested_changes: Keep sensor span at x = +/-0.05 m with 12 mm footprints for the next race, and report line_loss_events and whether runs end by completion, stall or off_track.
If max_error is near 0.06 with line loss gone, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same positions to add coverage margin beyond the current 0.0685 m reach.
If steering_oscillation rises once line loss is removed, try sensor y = 0.06 before changing the sensor span again.
